newsitem.title: USA: U.S. New England pipelines complete joint filing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. New England pipelines complete joint filing.

text.p: Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline LLC and Portland Natural Gas Transmission System have filed an abbreviated joint supplement with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission reflecting the companies' joint pipeline agreement announced in December, PanEnergy Corp said.

The filing Monday supplements the existing individual applications and seeks federal approval for the joint pipeline segment. The jointly owned pipeline, which represents an approximate 100-mile portion of the 729-mile Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline and the 290-mile PNGTS, is expected to have an in-service date of November 1, 1998.

The 1998 timeline coincides with the clearer picture of the need for new and replacement capacity for the Maine natural gas market, the timing of unbundling initiatives for gas service within Maine and the anticipated timing of the regulatory authorizations based upon the joint pipeline efforts with PNGTS, PanEnergy said.
The company is responsible for the overall development of the $975 million, 729-mile Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline project and is directly responsible for the United States portion of that project.
Westcoast Energy Inc is responsible for the development of the Canadian portion of project. Mobil Corp is also involved in the project.

The joint pipeline further ensures the Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline's scheduled in-service date of November 1999 is met. At that time, some 440 million cubic feet per day of firm natural gas transportation service will be available via the pipeline from Goldboro, Nova Scotia, to U.S. markets in Maine, New Hampshire and the Northeast.
The pipeline also will supply transportation capacity to serve markets in the Canadian Maritimes Provinces.

PNGTS is designed to transport natural gas from an interconnection with TransCanada PipeLines Ltd at the U.S./Canada border near Beecher Falls, Vt., to an interconnection with the with El Paso Energy Corp's Tennessee Gas Pipeline system.
Other PNGTS sponsors include Bay State Gas Co, Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP, MCN Corp and US Generating Co, a Bechtel Group Inc and Pacific Gas and Electric Co venture.
